provenance_note: Values recorded from the actual headline Kaggle run's split.py output log. NOT regenerated by rerunning split.py locally: this machine's data/raw/candidates.parquet (58,000 rows) is a different, older draw than the 75,000-pair pool the headline run actually used, so a local rerun would silently overwrite the real data/processed/*.parquet splits with a different, inconsistent dataset. This file documents the real run; it is not derived from local artifacts.
excluded_count_note: split.py's code now writes this field (tokenizer-pool rows plus any additional candidates sharing text with the pool), but its exact value for the real headline run was never captured in the saved log -- only candidate_pool_after_cleaning (the post-exclusion count) was recorded. Subtracting from an approximate pre-exclusion total would be an estimate, not a measured value, so this is left null rather than invented. Not required for dataset-composition correctness: the composition is fully determined by candidate_pool_after_cleaning, survived_max_len_filter, and the train/val/test sizes below, all of which are real recorded values.
target_leakage_diagnostic_note: split.py's code now computes and writes this field (train/val/test target-side overlap counts, diagnostic only, never enforced -- source-side disjointness remains the actual leakage protection, asserted and unchanged). This diagnostic was added to the code after the headline run already completed, so no measured value exists for the real headline split; it is left null here rather than invented or backfilled. It will be populated with real measured values the next time split.py actually runs against the real candidate pool.
